newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end lower with market stll nervous.
newsitem.headline: German shares end lower with market stll nervous.

text.p: German shares ended lower on Wednesday as worries re-emerged about excessive market strength, with Wall Street starting down and the dollar slipping, particularly weighing on German exporters.
The IBIS DAX, reflecting all-day electronic trade in the DAX index of 30 top German shares, ended down 54.59 points, or 1.89 percent at 2,836.36 points.

The Dow Jones index of U.S. blue-chip stocks started down nearly 100 points or around 1.5 percent, but then recovered to show a loss of around 83 points, helping the IBIS DAX come off a day's low of 2,819.68 points.
The DAX index had earlier ended bourse dealings down 49.95 points, or 1.73 percent, at 2,841.05.

Dealers said a fall on Friday, promted by comments by Federal Reserve chief Alan Greenspan about "irrational exuberance" in global asset markets, was still causing nerves and said some players were reassesing the significance of his statement.
"Greenspan is still making people edgy. We are extra-sensitive to any move down," said one trader.

By Tuesday the DAX had almost recouped all the losses posted on Friday rising up near the 2,900 point level and dealers said that markets had possibly recovered too quickly after the Greenspan warning.
"Greenspan did not say something like that for fun and he is a man who wants to be taken seriously," said one trader.
Dealers said that a Wall Street Journal article suggesting that a slowdown in Japanese purchases of U.S. debt could depress U.S. markets had also prompted fears.
Losses were spread across the board, with export-oriented chemicals and auto stocks especially hard hit as the dollar moved towards 1.54 marks, down a pfennig on Tuesday's level.
Shares in chemical company Bayer AG ended IBIS dealings down 2.57 marks, almost four percent, at 62.38 marks, while car maker BMW AG ended down almost three percent, or 30.70 marks at 1,040.30 marks.

Meanwhile, shares in chemicals and drugs company Hoechst AG ended down 34 pfennigs at 70.88, less than the market trend and much less than other chemical stocks after the firm made a buy out bid for French pharmaceuticals group Roussel Uclaf.
The stock had risen to a record high on Tuesday after the firm said it had merged its speciality chemicals division with the Swiss group Clariant AG.
